item.title: Influence of Agentic AI in Consumer Behaviour: Future Landscape
item.content:encoded:
Rahul Sindhwani, Indian Institute of Management – Sambalpur

Varsha Jain, ESSCA School of Management

Justin Zhang, University of North Florida

Sudhir Rana, Liwa University

This Special Issue aims to advance both theory and practice regarding consumer behavior in the age of agentic AI. Theoretically, it seeks to deepen understanding of how autonomous AI agents influence fundamental consumer processes such as decision-making, trust, perceived autonomy, and engagement.

Appel publié par Journal of Consumer Behaviour. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Consumer decision-making with autonomous AI agents
  • Trust in agentic AI systems
  • Perceived autonomy in AI-influenced consumer processes
  • Consumer engagement with autonomous AI agents
  • Theoretical frameworks for agentic AI and consumer behavior
  • Practical applications of agentic AI in consumer markets
  • Autonomous agents and fundamental consumer processes

item.title: Behavioural Environmental Economics & Policy (BEEP): trends and reflections
item.content:encoded:
Sanchayan Banerjee, King's College London

Lory Barile, University of Warwick

This special issue focuses on Behavioural Environmental Economics & Policy (BEEP), which examines how departures from rational choice assumptions—such as bounded rationality and bounded willpower—affect environmental decision-making and policy effectiveness. The issue seeks to consolidate evidence on how behavioural insights can improve the design and evaluation of environmental policies to address urgent challenges including climate change, biodiversity loss, and pollution.

The special issue welcomes conceptual, empirical, and policy-oriented contributions applying behavioural insights to environmental problems. Submissions may employ various methodologies including experiments, quasi-experimental designs, and literature reviews. The issue particularly values work that identifies both market and behavioural failures, designs and tests policies combining traditional instruments with behavioural tools, and evaluates their effectiveness and welfare impacts.

This is an invitation-only special issue in Environmental and Resource Economics.

Appel publié par Environmental and Resource Economics. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Interactions between market failures and behavioural failures in environmental settings
  • Policy design that combines prices/standards with behavioural tools (defaults, salience/framing, simplification, commitment)
  • Welfare analysis (including psychological costs), ethics, and paternalism in environmental policy
  • Empirical identification of behavioural mechanisms; field/lab/quasi-experimental evidence
  • Heterogeneity, equity, and distributional consequences of behavioural environmental policies
  • Replication, meta-analysis, and open-science practices in this domain
  • Choice architecture and environmental outcomes
  • Interactions between behavioural instruments and prices/regulation
  • Climate cognition and communication
  • Evaluation and methods

Timeline

  • November 30, 2026: Submission deadline

item.title: Multiple Objective Programming and Goal Programming: Artificial Intelligence for Decision Making in Economic and Social Sciences
item.content:encoded:
Matteo Rocca, University of Insubria

Davide La Torre, Skema Business School

Constantin Zopounidis, Technical University of Crete

This special issue brings together research at the intersection of multiple objective optimization, goal programming, and artificial intelligence to address complex decision-making problems in economic and social sciences. By combining structured methods for evaluating conflicting objectives with machine learning approaches that process large datasets, the issue seeks to advance both theoretical understanding and practical applications of these integrated methodologies.

The special issue welcomes original research papers, including substantially extended versions of presentations from the 16th International Conference on Multiple Objective Programming and Goal Programming (MOPGP'25, held July 1-3, 2025, in Varese, Italy), as well as papers not presented at the conference. Contributions should address theory or applications of multiple objective programming, goal programming, or artificial intelligence with relevance to economic or social decision-making contexts.

Appel publié par Annals of Operations Research. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

item.title: The evolution of decision-making and reasoning from childhood to adulthood
item.content:encoded:
,

,

This special issue examines how decision-making processes, choice behavior, and reasoning capabilities evolve from childhood through adulthood. Understanding the developmental trajectory of these fundamental cognitive and behavioral processes provides insight into the mechanisms that underlie human judgment and decision-making across the lifespan.

The collection seeks to integrate perspectives from developmental psychology, behavioral economics, cognitive science, and neuroscience to explore how individuals acquire, refine, and modify their decision-making strategies as they mature. Contributions may address the biological, cognitive, social, and environmental factors that shape the development of choice behavior and reasoning abilities.

Empirical studies, theoretical frameworks, and methodological approaches that advance our understanding of developmental decision-making are welcome. This includes research examining both normative development and individual variation in how people learn to make choices and engage in reasoning from early childhood through adulthood.

Appel publié par Journal of Behavioral and Experimental Economics. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Developmental changes in decision-making and choice behavior across the lifespan
  • Cognitive mechanisms underlying reasoning development
  • Economic decision-making in children and adolescents
  • The role of emotions and affect in developing choice behavior
  • Neural and biological substrates of reasoning development
  • Individual differences in decision-making trajectories
  • The impact of education and experience on choice behavior
  • Temporal and risk preferences across development
  • Social influences on reasoning and decision-making
  • Irrational choice patterns and their developmental origins

item.title: The Power of Difference: Strategic Decision-Making in Identity-Diverse Teams
item.content:encoded:
This special issue explores how identity diversity influences strategic decision-making processes within teams. We seek to understand the mechanisms through which diverse team compositions affect decision quality, creativity, and organizational outcomes. The focus is on examining both the benefits and challenges of managing identity-diverse teams in contemporary organizational settings.

Appel publié par Journal of Business Research. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Intersectionality and multiple dimensions of diversity
  • Cognitive and affective processes in diverse team settings
  • Organizational culture and inclusive practices
  • Leadership approaches in managing identity-diverse teams

item.title: AI-Driven Decision Making under Uncertain Environments: Theory, Methods, and Industrial Applications
item.content:encoded:
Hyun-Jung Kim, KAIST

Shu-Kai Fan, National Taipei University of Technology

Fugee Tsung, Hong Kong University of Science and Technology

Thomas Volling, Technical University Berlin

Jang Ho Kim, Korea University

Dong-Young Lim, Ulsan National Institute of Science and Technology

Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI), optimization, and data-driven analytics are fundamentally transforming decision-making processes in complex systems operating under uncertainty. Modern industrial and service systems, including manufacturing, logistics, supply chains, transportation, energy, and healthcare, increasingly face dynamic and stochastic environments characterized by demand fluctuations, disruptions, incomplete information, evolving system states, and operational risks. To effectively manage such complexity, there is growing interest in intelligent decision-making methodologies that integrate learning, prediction, optimization, simulation, and adaptation. In particular, emerging technologies such as reinforcement learning, foundation models, generative AI, agentic AI, digital twins, and hybrid AI-optimization frameworks are enabling the development of more autonomous, adaptive, and data-driven operational systems. Despite these advances, significant challenges remain regarding scalability, robustness, interpretability, real-time implementation, and the successful deployment of AI-driven decision-making approaches in real-world industrial environments.

Appel publié par International Journal of Production Research. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.
